blocks.heading: Zones 6, 7, 8, 9 & 10 Profile
blocks.intro: Detailed habitat breakdown and wildlife records for Ranthambore's buffer ranges.

items.title: Zone 6 (Kundal)
items.text: Scenic cliff landscapes, birds of prey, and dense dry scrub forests.
bullets: Key Landmarks: Kala Pani, Khabli, Patwa ki Baori, Saran Ka Patthar
Resident Wildlife: T-102 and cubs, T-39 lineage, Indian Gazelle (Chinkara), Sloth Bears
items.meta: Entry Gate: Rajbagh Naka / Kundal Gate

items.title: Zone 7 (Chhiddir)
items.text: High elevated plateaus with breathtaking panoramic views over the Aravali hills.
bullets: Key Landmarks: Rajbagh Naka, Chhiddir, Kushida, Jamun Deh
Resident Wildlife: Frequent leopard movement along escarpments, caracals, wild boars

items.title: Zone 8 (Balas)
items.text: Rugged wild terrain with dramatic gorges and tranquil natural pools.
bullets: Key Landmarks: Neemli Dang, Kali Bhat, Balas Plateau, Mahakho
Resident Wildlife: Territorial tigers, leopards, striped hyenas, honey badgers

items.title: Zone 9 (Kuwalji / Qualji)
items.text: Set along the banks of the Chambal river, offering combined forest and aquatic birding.
bullets: Key Landmarks: Kuwalji River Bank, 45km from Sawai Madhopur
Resident Wildlife: T-59 (Fateh lineage), Caracals, Sloth Bears, migratory waterfowl
items.meta: Entry Gate: Phalodi / Kuwalji Gate (Chambal River Route)

items.title: Zone 10 (Antri / Kushida)
items.text: Lush valley pockets and quiet uncrowded forest tracks loved by naturalists.
bullets: Key Landmarks: Halonda, Devpura Water Body, Antri, Bodal
Resident Wildlife: T-99, T-108, Nilgai herds, resident crocodiles in seasonal lakes

blocks.heading: Ranthambore Monsoon Safaris in Buffer Zones
blocks.intro: When core zones shut between July and September, nature flourishes with emerald greenery, cascading waterfalls, and active tiger movement in Buffer Zones 6, 7, 8, and 10. Monsoon safaris offer romantic mist, cloud-capped hills, and zero tourist crowd pressure.

items.title: Lush Greenery
items.text: Dramatic transformation from dry deciduous forest into a rainforest paradise.

items.title: Rainy Season Birding
items.text: Breeding plumage of Indian Pitta, Paradise Flycatcher, and Painted Storks.

items.title: Off-Season Tariff Discounts
items.text: Resorts offer up to 40% discount on luxury stays during monsoon months.

blocks.heading: Naturalist Tips for Buffer Zone Safaris

items.title: Scan High Rock Escarpments
items.text: Leopards in Zones 6, 7, and 8 frequently sunbathe on open rock ledges early in the morning before retreating into deep caves.

items.title: Listen for Deer Alarm Calls
items.text: In dense ravine tracks, animal calls (especially spotted deer and langurs) provide vital audio cues long before you see the predator.

items.title: Watch Waterhole Depressions
items.text: Natural springs like Kala Pani and Jamun Deh are perennial magnets for tigers, wild boars, and sloth bears during hot hours.

groups.title: Entry Regulations
items: Government photo identity verification is strictly enforced at every buffer gate entry post.
Gypsy drivers adhere to the 20 km/h forest speed limit to prevent sudden animal collisions.
Zones 6 to 10 are protected tiger reserve zones with identical legal protection under Project Tiger.
Littering or throwing plastic bottles on the trail is punishable by immediate fine and expulsion.

blocks.heading: Buffer Zones Safari FAQs
blocks.intro: Helpful facts about Zones 6 through 10 bookings.

items.q: Do tigers actually live in Buffer Zones 6 to 10?
items.a: Yes, absolutely! Tiger territories do not follow human demarcations. Zones 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 have permanent resident tiger populations with multiple breeding females, sub-adult cubs, and big territorial males.

items.q: Are Buffer Zone permits cheaper than Core Zones?
items.a: Rajasthan Forest Department charges the exact same standardized permit fee across all zones (1 through 10).

items.q: Can we take a Gypsy into Buffer Zones?
items.a: Both Maruti Gypsies and Canters operate across Zones 6 to 10 with certified forest department guides and drivers.

items.q: Are Buffer Zones open during the monsoon season?
items.a: Yes! While Core Zones 1 to 5 close from 1st July to 30th September for the breeding and monsoon season, several buffer gates (Zones 6, 7, 8, and 10) frequently remain open for tourists.
